questions.question:
Two statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically and definitely follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All donkeys are horses.

No cow is a horse.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some cows are donkeys

II. Some horses are donkeys.

III. No donkeys is a cow.

options.text: Both conclusions II and III follow
Either conclusion II or III follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d4d5265e0e05aa848f1797286b441aab207149af3f04361070498c63e5941931.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. Some cows are donkeys → False (All donkeys are horses and no cow is a horse, imply that no cows are donkeys)

II. Some horses are donkeys → True (All donkeys are horses imply that some horses are donkeys)

III. No donkeys is a cow → True (All donkeys are horses and no cow is a horse, imply that no donkeys are cow)

Hence, the correct answer is** ****Both conclusions II and III follow.**

questions.question:
Two statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some books are novels.

No novel is a diary.

**Conclusions:**

I. No book is a diary.

II. All diaries are books.

III. No diary is a novel.

options.text: Either conclusion I or II and only conclusion III follows.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a38f4cf3de409ac6a7a2b9fecf7c88e8fee630b0e01a4c04b2f2c4c8345ec301.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. No book is a diary → False (It is possible but not definite, as there is no direct relation between book and diary Therefore it is possible but not definite).

II. All diaries are books → False (It is possible but not definite, as there is no direct relation between book and diary Therefore it is possible but not definite)

III. No diary is a novel → True (No novel is a diary, imply that no diary is a novel)

When we combining the statement I and II we can not say that either I or II follows since, "**All and No" is not a complementary pair.**

Either conclusion 1 or 2 does not follow.

Only conclusion 3 will be follow.

Hence, the correct answer is **only conclusion III follows.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **__Confusion Points__**Conditions of Either-or case:

1. The elements should be the same in both statements.

2. Both the conclusions should be definitely false individually.

3. One conclusion should be positive and one conclusion should be negative (Complementary pair)

**The two complementary pairs are:**

**1) All + Some not**

**2) No + Some**

Note: All + No is not considered under Either -or case.
